paragraphs.text: The same Spirit of God that lifted up and acted the living weights and the wheels; like as the same breath causeth the diverse sounds in the organs.
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the Spirit lifted me up.

paragraphs.text: Of the outward court. {Eze 10:19}
paragraphs.anchor: Unto the east gate.

paragraphs.text: Proceres populi, the senators of the city, with their prefect or president. The like number is now at Rome, and likewise at London; an alderman in each of the twenty-four wards, and a mayor. See Rev 4:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Five and twenty men.

paragraphs.text: I saw them, and knew them by name; but for no good.
paragraphs.anchor: Among whom I saw Jaazaniah.

paragraphs.text: “ Iudex locusta civitatis est malus. ” - Scaliger.
That whet their wits and beat their brains about it; the politicians of the time, who, like children, are ever standing on their heads, and shaking their heels against heaven.
paragraphs.anchor: These are the men that devise mischief.

paragraphs.text: As Balaam and Ahithophel did of old, as Machiavel did at Florence, and Gondamor here did of later times. The prophet here nameth a couple, and taketh the same liberty to reprove them that they took to do amiss.
paragraphs.anchor: And give wicked counsel.

paragraphs.text: sc., The evil day is not. The vision that he seeth is for many days to come; and he prophesieth of the times that are far off. {Eze 12:22; Eze 12:27} See Amo 6:3 Isa 29:1 2Pe 3:4. And this was likely the evil counsel they gave the king and people, lulling them asleep in the cradle of carnal security.
paragraphs.anchor: Which say, It is not near

paragraphs.text: Though Jeremiah hath counselled us to the contrary, {Jer 29:5} though he, with all the wit he hath, hath told us that this city is the caldron, and we are the flesh. {Jer 1:13} Some such thing Jeremiah had indeed foretold, and these profane scoffers made a jeer at it. Captant argutias quibus elevant omnem fidem doctrinae coelestis. This made good Jeremiah complain heavily: Jer 20:7-8, "I am in derision daily, every one mocketh me," &c. Our prophet Ezekiel, though he name him not, yet confirmeth his holy sayings, and threateneth his scurrilous adversaries. Ministers should stand by and for one another.
paragraphs.anchor: Let us build houses.

paragraphs.text: Urger et repetit, ne cunctetur. Out of greatest indignation against these pests, he pricketh him on to prophesy, as having vengeance "in a readiness for the disobedient." {2Co 10:6} Mockers shall be sure to have their "bands increased." {Isa 28:22}
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy.

paragraphs.text: Et irruit in me Spiritus Iehovae; with force and power. It was a mighty lapse from a God much offended.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Spirit of the Lord fell upon me.

paragraphs.text: As Eze 11:3; but better ye had held your peace. Or, Thus have ye thought, and as good ye might have spake out.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus have ye said.

paragraphs.text: Heb., And the ascensions of your spirit, I know it; i.e., I know them every one, as if they had all been but one. I understand your ironies, your sly jeers and will deal with you accordingly. See Luk 24:38 Deu 31:21.
paragraphs.anchor: For I know the things that came into your mind.

paragraphs.text: Called therefore a bloody city, {Eze 22:2; Eze 9:9; Eze 7:23} and it shall therefore despume you; Vos sicut spumae eieciemini. Evil counsellors are cruel and bloody-minded; their craft is never but accompanied with cruelty, and their cruelty seldom without craft. "None of them wanteth their mate," as the Scripture speaks of those birds of prey and desolation. {Isa 34:16}
paragraphs.anchor: Ye have multiplied your slain in this city.

paragraphs.text: Whether ye have slain them outright, or have laid them bleeding and dying by your oppressions; for a poor man’s livelihood is his life. {Mar 12:44 Luk 8:43} He is in his house like a snail in his shell, crush that, and you kill him.
paragraphs.anchor: Your slain.

paragraphs.text: {a} Thus their own words, spoken in mockery, are wittily retorted upon them, and driven back again down their throats as it were.
paragraphs.anchor: And this city is the caldron.

paragraphs.text: As rotten flesh, to be cast out; or as filthy scum, to boil over.
paragraphs.anchor: But I will bring you forth out of the midst of it.

paragraphs.text: {a} Haec verba monachi funibus trahunt ad purgatorium probandum, nixi autoritate Originis.
And yet they made as if they feared nothing; they doubted not but to die in their nest; but all guilt hath fear, and all such fear hath torment.
paragraphs.anchor: Ye have feared the sword.

paragraphs.text: Such as all your craft can never keep off. Ineluctabilis vis fatorum, cuius fortunam mutare canstituit, consilia corrumpit. {a} See Pro 10:24. {See Trapp on "Pro 10:24"}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will bring a sword upon you.

paragraphs.text: {a} Velleius, lib. ii.
The same again, for better assurance. We use to do so oft when we threaten aught.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will bring you out of the midst thereof.

paragraphs.text: In the northern border, even at Riblah. {2Ki 25:6; 2Ki 25:21 Jer 52:10; Jer 52:24; Jer 52:27}
paragraphs.anchor: I will judge you in the border of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Ye shall not be so happy as to die in your own native country, atque ante ora patrum {a} but elsewhere, at Riblah or Antiochia.
paragraphs.anchor: This city shall not be your caldron.

paragraphs.text: {a} Virgil.
That which ye would not take knowledge of by the words of your prophets, ye shall now be made to know by the swords of your enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall know that I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: When God is about to proceed in judgment against evildoers, there is ever a cause for it, and they shall know it.
paragraphs.anchor: For ye have not walked in my statutes.

paragraphs.text: God heweth men by his prophets, and slayeth them by the words of his mouth, and his judgments are as the light, or lightning, that goeth forth. {Hos 6:5} Elisha hath his sword as well as Jehu and Hazael. {1Ki 19:17} See Jer 1:10 2Co 10:6.
paragraphs.anchor: And it came to pass that when I prophesied.

paragraphs.text: Suddenly, {a} and before his time, in Solomon’s sense. {Ecc 7:17} Driven away he was in his iniquity Cerinthus, Arius so were Ananias and Sapphira, Cerinthus, Arius, Stephen Gardiner, Cardinal Pool, Dick of Dover, as they called the persecuting suffragan {b} there; Nightingale, parson of Becking, &c. See Pro 6:14-15.
paragraphs.anchor: Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died.

paragraphs.text: Out of a holy solicitude about God’s elect, lest they also should have perished, as Petaliah had done, whose very name might seem somewhat ominous, for it signifieth "the escaped one of the Lord"; and therefore his sudden death might portend destruction to the remnant of Israel.
paragraphs.anchor: Then fell I down upon my face.

paragraphs.text: Sudden or singular judgments put saints upon humble, earnest, and argumentative prayer.
paragraphs.anchor: And cried with a loud voice.

paragraphs.text: {a} Magnum est subito opprimi.
{b} A bishop considered in regard to his relation to the archbishop or metropolitan, by whom he may be summoned to attend synods and give his suffrage. ŒD
In answer to my prayer, though there was something in it of unbelief and human frailty. See Psa 31:22. {See Trapp on "Psa 31:22"}
paragraphs.anchor: Again the word of the Lord came unto me.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Thine unbrotherly brethren of Jerusalem seek to unbrother and to unchurch thee and the rest of thy fellow captives. See Isa 65:5. Papists and sectaries deal so by us.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy brethren, even thy brethren

paragraphs.text: Viri vindiciarum tuarum, or they that have the right of redemption.
paragraphs.anchor: The men of thy kindred.

paragraphs.text: Tota domus Israelis, quanta quanta est. The Jerusalemites challenged the Lord, and the land, and all therein, to be theirs, excluding, and as it were excommunicating, the captives at Babylon, who were dear to God. So dealt the scribes and Pharisees by the Christians; {Joh 16:2 Act 26:9-11} so did the Rogatian heretics and the Donatists, who gave themselves out, as now the Papists do, to be the only Catholics. The Arians called the orthodox, by way of scorn and contempt, Ambrosians, Athanasians, Homousians, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And all the house of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Gressus removete, profani: Ita in malam crucem: εις κορακας. Ye are cut off from the people of God, and may go whither you will; we are heirs and owners of the promises, ye are outcasts and abjects.
paragraphs.anchor: Get ye far from the Lord.

paragraphs.text: What a cornucopia of comfort may this promise be to poor prisoners, forlorn exiles, and such as by sickness or otherwise are necessitated to keep from public ordinances, that they shall have God’s presence and protection, the comfort and conduct of his Spirit, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Although I have cast them.

paragraphs.text: Sanctuarium modicum. By heating their prayers, sanctifying their natures, bringing to their remembrance what things they have heard and learned touching me and my will, themselves and their duties. They should in Babylon worship God in spirit and in truth; and in the life to come the Lord God Almighty and his Lamb should be their temple. {Rev 21:22}
paragraphs.anchor: Yet I will be to them as a little sanctuary.

paragraphs.text: How impossible or improbable soever you may think it, and those of Jerusalem pronounce it. The prophet Isaiah in many chapters of his gospel, which beginneth at Eze 40:1-49, setteth himself to cheer up these poor captives with good hopes of a return, after a little while, paulisper, as some render the word megnat in the foregoing Eze 11:16.
paragraphs.anchor: I will even gather you from the people.

paragraphs.text: So God calleth their idols and monuments of idolatry, not deigning to call them by their usual names. After the captivity the Jews would never endure idols. They chose rather to die than to suffer Caligula’s statue to be set up in their temple by Petronins. To this day they say that there is an ounce of the golden calf in all their sufferings.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall take away all the detestable things.

paragraphs.text: Opposed to a "divided heart," such as the Paphlagonian partridges are said to have; {Hos 10:2} that is, partly for God, and partly for the world. {Eze 33:31} This oneness of heart truly and entirely cleaving to God alone, is that boon that David so dearly beggeth, {Psa 86:11} that he might attend upon God without distraction. {1Co 7:35} And as the visible beams are wholly bent upon the thing that is beheld by the eye, and as it were concentred in it, {a} so might his desires and endeavours be entirely carried toward God, and firmly fixed upon him.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will give them one heart.

paragraphs.text: The same soul for substance, but altered in the frame, renewed in the qualities thereof. {Mar 16:17} They shall "speak with new tongues"; so we read of a "new song"; the strings are the same, but the tune is changed. See Psa 51:12 Eph 4:23 2Co 5:17.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will put a new spirit within you.

paragraphs.text: Extraham, say the Septuagint. I will draw or pull it out, which none can do but the hand of Heaven. God only can make the flinty heart fleshly, that is, sensible, soft, pliant, penetrable, buxom, and obedient to his holy will.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will take away the stony heart.

paragraphs.text: {a} Plin., lib. xi. cap. 37.
The covenant of grace is suited to all the exigencies and indigencies of a poor saint. It is "ordered in all things." {2Sa 23:5}
paragraphs.anchor: That they may walk in my statutes.

paragraphs.text: This is added lest any wicked men should misapply the promises, as they do qui sperando praesumunt et praesumendo pereunt.
paragraphs.anchor: But as for them.

paragraphs.text: Now God is utterly leaving the refractory Jews. He did so much more after their rejection of Christ and his gospel.
paragraphs.anchor: Then did the cherubims.

paragraphs.text: From the east gate.
paragraphs.anchor: From the midst of the city.

paragraphs.text: Mount Olivet. There he made his last stand, to see if they would meet him with entreaties of peace, that he might stop or step back. Here it was that Christ wept over the city, and hence he went up to heaven; after which came the Romans and destroyed it.
paragraphs.anchor: And stood upon the mountain.

paragraphs.text: i.e., In a supernatural rapture.
paragraphs.anchor: By the Spirit of God

paragraphs.text: These were his proper charge, and now God’s chiefest care. To them therefore he delivered the whole counsel of God, which he had seen and heard for their better settlement.
paragraphs.anchor: Then I spake unto them of the captivity.
